parts.name: Skull
parts.what: The skull is a hard shell that protects your brain and holds your eyes, ears and teeth in place. It is made of several bones joined together.
illnesses: Head injuries from falls and motorbike crashes
warnings: Head knock followed by vomiting, confusion or sleepiness
Clear fluid leaking from the nose or ear after a fall
Sudden severe headache
prevention: Wear a helmet on a motorbike or bicycle
Make floors and stairs safe from slips
Brush and see a dentist every year

parts.name: Spine
parts.what: The spine is a stack of small bones that holds your body up and lets you bend and twist. It also surrounds and protects the spinal cord, the main cable that carries messages to the body.
illnesses: Low back pain from heavy lifting
Osteoporosis, where bones become thin and weak
warnings: Back pain with leg weakness or numbness
Trouble holding urine or stool
Back pain after a fall, or that wakes you at night with fever
prevention: Lift with your knees, not your back
Walk every day and stay active
Eat foods with calcium and get some morning sun

parts.name: Rib cage
parts.what: The ribs curve around your chest like a cage. They guard the heart and lungs and move a little each time you breathe.
illnesses: Bruised or cracked ribs after a fall
Tuberculosis that spreads to the chest wall
warnings: Sharp chest pain that gets worse when you breathe in
Chest pain with shortness of breath
Coughing blood
prevention: Prevent falls at home
Do not smoke
Finish TB medicine fully if you were prescribed it

parts.name: Arm bones
parts.what: Three long bones in each arm, the upper arm bone and two forearm bones, let you reach, lift and carry. They join at the shoulder, elbow and wrist.
illnesses: Arthritis in the shoulder or elbow
warnings: A bent or swollen arm after a fall
A joint that is red, hot and very painful
Numb fingers that do not go away
prevention: Keep walkways dry and well lit
Drink less alcohol and limit organ meats if you have gout
Do light stretching daily

parts.name: Pelvis
parts.what: The pelvis is the wide ring of bone at your hips. It carries the weight of your upper body and protects the bladder and other organs below the belly.
warnings: Cannot stand or walk after a fall
Groin or hip pain that gets worse over weeks
A leg that looks shorter or turned outward
prevention: Use grab bars and non-slip mats
Do balance and strength exercise
Ask your doctor about a bone density check after 50

parts.name: Leg bones
parts.what: The thigh bone is the longest and strongest bone in your body. With the shin bone it carries your weight when you stand, walk and climb.
illnesses: Rickets in children who lack vitamin D or calcium
warnings: Knee swollen, hot and locking
Pain when putting weight on the leg after a fall
One calf swollen and painful
prevention: Keep a healthy weight to ease the knees
Wear shoes with a good grip
Give children milk, fish and some sunshine

parts.name: Neck and shoulders
parts.what: These muscles hold your head up and let you shrug, turn and lift your arms. They often tighten when you are tired or stressed.
illnesses: Stiff neck from poor sleeping position
warnings: Neck stiffness with high fever and headache
Arm pain with chest tightness
Shoulder that cannot move at all
prevention: Use a pillow that keeps your neck straight
Take breaks from the phone and screens
Stretch gently in the morning

parts.name: Chest muscles
parts.what: The chest muscles pull your arms forward and help you push and lift. Small muscles between the ribs also help you breathe.
warnings: Chest pressure, sweating or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
Pain with shortness of breath
Blistering rash in a band around one side
prevention: Warm up before heavy work
Do not lift very heavy loads alone
Ask your doctor about the shingles vaccine

parts.name: Belly and core
parts.what: The belly muscles hold your organs in place and support your back. A strong core helps you sit, stand and bend with less pain.
illnesses: Hernia, a bulge where the wall is weak
Back pain from a weak core
warnings: A bulge that is painful, hard or will not go back in
Belly pain with vomiting
Sudden swelling in the groin
prevention: Keep a healthy weight
Eat enough fiber so you do not strain on the toilet
Do gentle core exercise like walking and bridges

parts.name: Arm muscles
parts.what: The muscles at the front and back of your upper arm bend and straighten your elbow. They help you carry bags, pour water and push up from a chair.
illnesses: Tennis elbow, pain on the outer elbow
warnings: Sudden weakness in one arm
Arm pain with a snap and bruising
Weakness on one side of the face and body
prevention: Eat enough protein such as fish, egg and beans
Do light weight or water-bottle lifts
Rest when a muscle is sore

parts.name: Thigh muscles
parts.what: The big muscles at the front and back of your thigh straighten and bend your knee. They are what you use to stand up, climb stairs and walk.
illnesses: Muscle loss with age, which raises the risk of falls
Muscle pain from some cholesterol medicine
warnings: Severe muscle pain with dark urine
One thigh or calf swollen, red and warm
Sudden weakness in both legs
prevention: Walk daily and practice sitting down and standing up
Drink enough water
Tell your doctor about muscle pain from medicine

parts.name: Calf muscles
parts.what: The calf muscles lift your heel and push you forward with each step. They also help squeeze blood in the leg veins back up toward the heart.
illnesses: Leptospirosis from floodwater, which causes calf pain
Blood clot in a leg vein
warnings: Fever and severe calf pain after wading in floodwater
One leg swollen, red and sore
Sudden shortness of breath with leg pain
prevention: Avoid wading in floodwater, or wear boots
Move your legs on long trips
Stretch calves before bed

parts.name: Heart
parts.what: The heart is a strong muscle about the size of your fist. It pumps blood to the whole body all day and night, bringing oxygen and food to every part.
illnesses: Rheumatic heart disease after untreated strep throat
warnings: Chest pressure or pain lasting more than a few minutes
Pain spreading to the arm, back or jaw
Cold sweat, nausea or sudden breathlessness
prevention: Check your blood pressure often
Eat less salt, fried food and sweet drinks
Do not smoke and walk 30 minutes most days

parts.name: Blood vessels
parts.what: Arteries carry blood from the heart out to the body and veins bring it back. Blood carries oxygen, food and the cells that fight germs.
illnesses: Stroke, when blood cannot reach part of the brain
Dengue, which can cause leaking vessels and low platelets
warnings: Face drooping, arm weakness or slurred speech
Fever with bleeding gums, black stool or belly pain
A leg that is cold, pale or very painful
prevention: Take blood pressure medicine every day
Remove standing water to stop dengue mosquitoes
Keep sugar and cholesterol in range

parts.name: Lungs
parts.what: The lungs take in air, move oxygen into your blood and send carbon dioxide out. You have two, and the right one is slightly bigger than the left.
illnesses: COPD, often from smoking or cooking smoke
warnings: Cough lasting more than two weeks
Coughing blood, or night sweats with weight loss
Fast breathing, blue lips or chest pulling in
prevention: Do not smoke and avoid smoky kitchens
Get flu and pneumonia vaccines
Cover your cough and finish TB treatment

parts.name: Windpipe
parts.what: The windpipe is the tube that carries air from your throat down to the lungs. It splits into two smaller tubes, one for each lung.
warnings: Cannot speak or breathe while eating
Noisy, high-pitched breathing
Cough that brings up yellow or green mucus with fever
prevention: Chew slowly and sit upright when eating
Keep small objects away from toddlers
Wash hands often

parts.name: Brain
parts.what: The brain controls your thoughts, memory, feelings, movement and senses. It also keeps your heart beating and your breathing going without you thinking.
warnings: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side
Trouble speaking or seeing suddenly
Worst headache of your life or a seizure
prevention: Control blood pressure and sugar
Sleep 7 to 8 hours and stay social
Wear a helmet and do not drink and drive

parts.name: Spinal cord
parts.what: The spinal cord runs down the middle of your spine and carries messages between the brain and the rest of the body. Nerves branch off it to every limb.
warnings: Sudden weakness or numbness in both legs
Loss of control of bladder or bowel
Back pain with fever and weight loss
prevention: Wear seat belts and helmets
Prevent falls
Treat back pain that keeps getting worse

parts.name: Nerves
parts.what: Nerves are thin cables that run through your arms and legs. They send touch, pain and temperature to the brain and tell your muscles to move.
illnesses: Diabetic neuropathy, numb or burning feet
Leprosy, which is rare but still found
warnings: Numb feet or sores you do not feel
Burning or tingling that spreads
Patch of skin that has lost feeling
prevention: Keep blood sugar in range
Check your feet every day if you have diabetes
Do not stay in one hand position for hours

parts.name: Stomach
parts.what: The stomach is a stretchy bag that mixes food with acid and starts to break it down. After a few hours it passes the food to the intestines.
illnesses: Gastritis and ulcers, often from H. pylori germs or pain medicine
warnings: Vomiting blood or black stool
Belly pain that does not ease
Weight loss and trouble swallowing
prevention: Eat on time and do not skip meals
Avoid too much NSAID pain medicine
Wash food and hands well

parts.name: Liver
parts.what: The liver cleans your blood, makes bile to digest fat and stores energy. It is the body's main filter and can repair itself when treated well.
illnesses: Schistosomiasis in some areas of the Philippines
warnings: Yellow skin or eyes
Dark urine and pale stool
Swollen belly or vomiting blood
prevention: Get the hepatitis B vaccine
Limit alcohol
Avoid raw shellfish, wash hands, drink safe water

parts.name: Small intestine
parts.what: The small intestine is a long coiled tube where most food is broken down and its nutrients move into your blood. It is about as long as a bus.
warnings: Diarrhea with dry mouth, very little urine or dizziness
Fever with belly pain for several days
Blood in the stool
prevention: Drink safe water and wash hands before eating
Cook food well
Take deworming tablets as advised

parts.name: Large intestine
parts.what: The large intestine takes water out of what is left after digestion and forms stool. It ends at the rectum, where stool waits to leave the body.
warnings: Pain starting near the navel then moving to the lower right belly
Blood in the stool or black stool
Change in bowel habits lasting weeks
prevention: Eat vegetables, fruit and whole grains
Drink water and move daily
Ask about colon screening from age 45 to 50

parts.name: Kidneys
parts.what: Your two kidneys clean your blood, remove extra water and waste as urine, and help control blood pressure. Each is about the size of a fist, behind the belly on each side of the spine.
illnesses: Chronic kidney disease, often from diabetes or high blood pressure
warnings: Swollen feet or face
Much less urine, or foamy or bloody urine
Pain in the side or back with fever
prevention: Keep blood pressure and sugar in range
Drink enough water
Avoid NSAID pain medicine unless your doctor says it is safe for you, and herbal products of unknown content

parts.name: Bladder
parts.what: The bladder is a muscle bag that stores urine until you are ready to pass it. When it is full, nerves tell you to go.
warnings: Burning when passing urine, or going very often
Cannot pass urine at all
Blood in the urine or fever with back pain
prevention: Drink water through the day
Do not hold urine for long
Wipe front to back and keep the area clean

parts.name: Skin
parts.what: The skin is your largest organ. It keeps germs out, holds water in, helps control body heat and lets you feel touch.
warnings: A mole that changes shape, color or size
A wound that does not heal in weeks
Red skin spreading fast with fever
prevention: Bathe and dry well, especially folds
Use sunscreen and a hat in strong sun
Do not share towels and clean small cuts

parts.name: Hair and nails
parts.what: Hair helps keep your head warm and protected. Nails guard your fingertips and toes. Both grow from living cells under the skin and can show how healthy you are.
warnings: Dark streak under a nail
Nail that is thick, painful or leaking pus
Patches of hair loss with a red or scaly scalp
prevention: Keep nails short and clean
Wear slippers in public showers
Eat enough protein, iron and vitamins

parts.name: Pituitary gland
parts.what: This pea-sized gland under the brain is the boss of the hormone system. It tells other glands, like the thyroid and adrenals, when to make more or less.
illnesses: Pituitary growth that presses on vision
Too little or too much growth hormone
Low thyroid hormone due to pituitary problems
warnings: Long-lasting headache with changes in vision
Severe tiredness, weakness and weight change
Missed periods with breast milk when not pregnant
prevention: Most pituitary problems cannot be prevented
See a doctor early for unusual symptoms
Wear a helmet to avoid head injury

parts.name: Thyroid
parts.what: The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland in the front of the neck. Its hormones set how fast your body uses energy, and affect heart rate, weight and mood.
illnesses: Goiter (swollen neck), often from too little iodine
warnings: Lump or swelling in the front of the neck
Racing heart, shaking, weight loss with a good appetite
Always cold, very tired, weight gain, dry skin
prevention: Use iodized salt
Do not smoke
Get a blood test if a family member has thyroid disease

parts.name: Pancreas
parts.what: The pancreas sits behind the stomach. It makes insulin, the hormone that moves sugar from your blood into your cells, and juices that help digest food.
illnesses: Pancreatitis, often from gallstones or heavy drinking
warnings: Very thirsty, urinating often, blurry vision
Severe upper belly pain that goes to the back
Wounds that heal slowly or tingling feet
prevention: Keep a healthy weight and move daily
Eat less sugar and smaller rice portions
Limit alcohol and get a sugar test if you are over 40

parts.name: Adrenal glands
parts.what: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys. They make stress hormones, such as cortisol, that help you handle illness, danger and changes in blood pressure.
illnesses: Too much cortisol, which can cause weight gain, high sugar and high blood pressure
warnings: Very low blood pressure with fainting and vomiting
Round face, new purple stretch marks and weak muscles
Sudden spells of pounding headache and sweating
prevention: Never stop steroid medicine suddenly without your doctor
Keep up blood pressure checks
Manage stress with sleep, rest and exercise
